## Description

In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to transform standard `ggplot2` outputs into clear, polished, publication-ready figures. Working through practical examples, we will cover:

- choosing and customizing color scales and themes (e.g. colorblind-safe palettes)
- improving typography and annotations (e.g. with `ggtext` or `ggrepel`)
- combining plots into multi-panel layouts (e.g. with `patchwork`)
- exporting figures at the resolution and dimensions journals expect

Along the way I will show you a few useful extension packages from the `ggplot2` ecosystem and you will learn techniques you can apply directly to your own plots.

**Format:** 2-hour hands-on workshop. You'll follow along on your own computer.

## Workshop materials

All demo scripts and exercises are in the workshop repo:

[github.com/selinazitrone/advanced-ggplot-workshop](https://github.com/selinazitrone/advanced-ggplot-workshop)

Before the workshop, clone the repo, open the project, and run `source("install_packages.R")`.

## Resources and links

### Books and tutorials

- [ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis (Wickham et al.)](https://ggplot2-book.org/) — the canonical reference
- [Cédric Scherer's tutorials](https://www.cedricscherer.com/) — the modern `ggplot2` reference, full of polished examples
- [Albert Rapp's blog](https://albert-rapp.de/) — practical, well-explained data viz with R
- [R Graphics Cookbook (Chang)](https://r-graphics.org/) — recipe-style problems and answers
- [Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction (Healy)](https://socviz.co/) — theory plus `ggplot2` code

### Packages covered in the workshop

- [`ggtext`](https://wilkelab.org/ggtext) — markdown/HTML in titles, labels, and legends
- [`ggrepel`](https://ggrepel.slowkow.com/) — non-overlapping text labels
- [`gghighlight`](https://yutannihilation.github.io/gghighlight/) — one-line subset highlighting
- [`patchwork`](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com) — multi-panel layouts
- [`colorblindr`](https://github.com/clauswilke/colorblindr) — colorblindness simulation
- [`paletteer`](https://emilhvitfeldt.github.io/paletteer/) — a meta-package wrapping ~2500 palettes
- [`scales`](https://scales.r-lib.org/) — axis label and break formatting
- [`ragg`](https://ragg.r-lib.org/) — high-quality plot renderer
- [`ggview`](https://github.com/idmn/ggview) — preview plots at their export size

### Honorable mentions

- [`ggdist`](https://mjskay.github.io/ggdist/) — raincloud, halfeye, dotsinterval plots
- [`ggsignif`](https://const-ae.github.io/ggsignif/) and [`ggpubr`](https://rpkgs.datanovia.com/ggpubr/) — significance brackets and p-values
- [`ggridges`](https://wilkelab.org/ggridges) — ridgeline plots
- [`ggh4x`](https://teunbrand.github.io/ggh4x/) — nested facets and custom strips
- [`ggExtra`](https://github.com/daattali/ggExtra) — marginal histograms and densities
- [`cowplot`](https://wilkelab.org/cowplot/) — patchwork's older sibling, with extra helpers

### Tools for checking your figures

- [Snook.ca color-contrast tool](https://snook.ca/technical/colour_contrast/colour.html) — check contrast
- [Viz Palette tool](https://projects.susielu.com/viz-palette) — preview a palette for colorblindness
